children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This would include things like full-time non-advanced education such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or approved training programs.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. So Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which is approved education.

Now I need to understand your living situation:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand if you're still responsible for him financially.

**Are you making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** (This could include money for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributions towards his accommodation - and it would need to be at least the same amount as Child Benefit, which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child or £16.95 per week for additional children.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with his clothes, food, and other expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute per week (or per month) towards Alex's upkeep?** I need to understand if it's at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount, which is £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards his expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful.

Now I need to confirm a few more details:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - he's focused on his studies. And he's not claiming any benefits in his own right either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 18, he's still eligible because he's in approved education (studying for his A-levels at sixth form college). Child Benefit can continue until age 20 for young people in approved education or training.

✅ **You're responsible for him** - Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit amount (£25.60 per week for an eldest/only child). This means you're still considered responsible for him.

✅ **Other criteria met** - You live in the UK, no one else is claiming for Alex, and he's not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit on the government website. If your circumstances change (such as Alex finishing his education or you stopping your contributions), you'll need to inform HMRC.
